question: Should OpenClaw core accept a persisted user-configured OTLP diagnostics surface and shared instrumentation API before a broader instrumentation plan exists?
rationale: The implementation is opt-in and bounded, but it establishes permanent core configuration, runtime dependencies, and privacy conventions whose acceptance cannot be inferred from mechanical correctness alone.

options.title: Accept Bounded Groundwork
options.body: Approve the probe-only endpoint and shared helpers after the delivery-state defect is fixed and refreshed current-main validation passes.

options.title: Keep Docs, Defer Runtime
options.body: Retain the telemetry boundary design but defer packages, settings, UI, and helper APIs until a concrete instrumentation use case is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Accept Bounded Groundwork
recommendation.body: Approve the probe-only endpoint and shared helpers after the delivery-state defect is fixed and refreshed current-main validation passes.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing diagnostics surface, SettingsManager baseline, App composition, and related test infrastructure trace most strongly to this owner in current-main history.
